root_idea.summary: The root centers on removing hair or a superficial covering, with related extensions to circular forms and elevation.
root_idea.development: Classical lexical development proceeds from shaving or stripping away to destruction and roughness; from circular form to rings, enclosures, and ring-shaped marks; and from circling or rising to height and elevated places.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the independent anatomical noun حُلْقُوم.
Displayed under the singular active-participle citation form مُحَلِّق rather than the Quranic plural مُحَلِّقِينَ.

senses.definition: To shave the hair from the head.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb appears in the construction نَحْلِقَ الرُّؤُوسَ, referring to shaving the head.

senses.definition: The throat, especially the windpipe or air passage.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic expression places the departing soul at the throat; classical descriptions distinguish حُلْقُومٌ as especially the windpipe while allowing broader throat usage.

senses.definition: One who shaves; shaving or having shaved the head.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural مُحَلِّقِينَ describes people who have shaved their heads. The Form II formation can convey the action applied to multiple objects or with an intensive sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the imprecation عَقْرًا حَلْقًا or عَقْرَى حَلْقَى, an expression associated with bereavement and the shaving of a woman's hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The authorities report variant explanations, including wishing throat pain and describing an unlucky or troublesome woman; these are interpretations of the idiom rather than separate ordinary meanings of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional expression for trial, trouble, distress, or calamity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the phrase بَيْنَهُمُ اِحْلِقِي وَقُومِي and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shear or remove the hair of a goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classically distinguished from جَزَّ, which is used especially for shearing sheep's wool.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To peel, scrape, pare, or strip away a thing's superficial part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive extension of removing an outer covering, synonymous with قَشَرَ in this use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy or cut off completely, as a razor removes hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative or extended usage; the object is understood from context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or injure the throat, or to suffer pain or a complaint in the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be transitive when someone is made to suffer throat pain and intransitive when a person suffers such pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a watering-trough or tank up to its throat or upper filling level.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use with troughs and tanks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a thing according to a measure or proportion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical variant equated with خَلَقَ in this specialized usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an udder, to rise toward the belly and become contracted, with the milk becoming scant or withdrawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage has a contrastive counterpart in which the udder is full or abundantly milked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an udder, to be full or large and abundant in milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same lexical family is also reported with the opposite udder condition, namely contraction and scant milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ring, circle, loop, or circular formation; by extension a ring of people, a ring or link of mail, a rope loop, arms or armor, or a ring-shaped brand on camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The circular sense applies to objects, groups arranged in a ring, and marks or equipment made in a ring form. The associated Form II verb can mean to sit in circles or to put something into a ringed covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw or turn a circle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II action of producing a circular line or form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cancel a person's stipend, pay, or allowance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic Form II construction, probably extended from drawing a line around a name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the moon, to have a halo or ring around it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II usage describing a circular atmospheric appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird, to soar and circle in flight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes elevated circular movement through the air.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rise high or be overhead; a high or overtopping place or mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of celestial bodies, elevated places, and high mountains; the plural may denote the open spaces between heaven and earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise one's eyes toward the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II construction with the gaze directed upward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withdraw or diminish; of milk, to recede, and of water in a trough, to become scant or go away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Form II usage of liquids or stored water, distinct from the ordinary act of shaving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels' eyes, to sink or become depressed in their heads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of the eyes' sunken appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dates, to become ripe as far as a specified portion, commonly about two-thirds, or to begin ripening near the base.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reports vary over whether the relevant portion is near the base or the two-thirds stage; partly ripe dates are included in the usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a draught, to cause the belly to become inflated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized idiomatic use with a milk-and-water draught.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw or cast a thing to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II construction governing the recipient with إِلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of hair, to come off as though it had been shaved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form VII result, describing hair loss rather than the agent's shaving action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or sever a person's throat or windpipe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized quadriliteral formation based on حُلْقُومٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fauces, throat, or front part of the neck; the place of slaughter in an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical descriptions distinguish the fauces and throat from the windpipe, while noting overlap in ordinary usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The channel or part through which water runs in a vessel, watering-trough, or tank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the throat or passage of the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Watercourses, valleys, or narrow passages of a land or road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural usage extended from channels and constricted passages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper region of the air.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative spatial use of حَلْقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unlucky or destructive to others, as though stripping them away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended evaluative use, also applied to a year or circumstance that destroys what it encounters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bereavement through the death of a child; by association, the shaving of the head in such mourning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun used in a proverbial expression and connected with customary mourning practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Numerous cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The metaphor is explained by the way grazing animals crop vegetation as shaving removes hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A king's signet ring; by extension, the authority or office conferred by it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated expression can mean that someone was made a governor, commander, or similar official.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ring-like anatomical opening, including a ring of the womb or the anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Technical anatomical usage; the two rings of the womb are described in relation to its openings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper portion or filling level of a vessel or watering-trough, commonly the part above half-full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported extent ranges from the portion above half to the full level or somewhat less, depending on the vessel and authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Faucial, guttural, or pertaining to the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In grammatical terminology, حروف حلقية are the six guttural letters assigned to different parts of the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Death, conceived as stripping people away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An indeclinable epithet used in expressions such as the cup of death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act or occurrence of shaving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This nominal use denotes the act itself rather than the person who performs it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shaven; having the hair removed, of a head, hair, beard, or she-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing the resulting state after shaving or shearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hair shorn from a goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the removed hair or the shearing product.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shaver or shearer; specifically, one who shaves hair in connection with affliction or mourning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to a head wound that scrapes skin from flesh, treated separately below.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wound of the head that scrapes away the skin from the flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for a type of head wound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sharp or keen; of a knife, sword, person, or penetrating gaze.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The gaze usage describes looking intently or sharply.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick, swift, light, active, or agile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended descriptive adjective for movement or bodily action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean, slender, or lank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general bodily description, without restricting the referent to a particular animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tendril or twining portion of a grapevine, colocynth, or similar plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is motivated by its circular or curling form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year of drought, barrenness, or dearth that destroys what it encounters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized feminine adjective used of a destructive season or calamity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The severing or abandonment of kinship; mutual wronging and evil-speaking; or conduct that destroys and cuts off religion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional moral and social usage, described as a destructive disease among peoples.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A razor or instrument used for shaving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun names the implement rather than the act of shaving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A very rough garment whose texture removes or abrades hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the garment's hair-shaving roughness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place of head-shaving in Mina.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-name or geographical designation associated with the shaving rite.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel that is less than full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive participle for a vessel whose contents do not reach full capacity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean or emaciated, especially of sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-specific adjectival use distinct from the broader adjective حَالِقٌ meaning lean or slender.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert in which there is no water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized or descriptive use of the active participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To utter the formula لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized verb formed from the expression; another reported form is حَوْقَلَ.

cautions: The Quranic form مُحَلِّقِينَ is presented under the singular active-participle citation form مُحَلِّق.
Classical descriptions overlap حَلْقٌ and حُلْقُومٌ in ordinary throat usage, although حَلْقٌ is often associated with the fauces and حُلْقُومٌ with the windpipe.
The lexical discussion of حَلَقَ الضَّرْعُ explicitly reports opposite meanings—an udder becoming contracted and an udder being full—so both branches are retained separately.
